2607.28528.title: AI systems and the reproduction of (standard) language ideologies in World Englishes
2607.28528.paper_summary: The rapid growth of large language models (LLMs) has resurrected age-old questions in sociolinguistics and world Englishes, such as who decides what counts as legitimate English, whose English is suspect etc. This paper examines how AI systems, their uses and discourse on them reflect, reinforce, and occasionally challenge (standard) language ideologies, which privilege Inner Circle norms and marginalize non-dominant Englishes. Drawing on evidence from empirical studies, media commentary, social media debates, and examples from AI outputs, the paper shows that AI technologies reproduce dominant language ideologies at different levels: training data, design protocols, evaluation benchmarks, user feedback and public commentary. The analysis uses the public controversy over AI-sounding language, especially the fixation on the word delve, to illustrate how speakers of English from the Global North police the English language norms of Global South English users. The paper also identifies what Christian Mair has called a "standardisation paradox": AI may homogenize English by privileging standard forms and at the same time pluralize Englishes through exposure to wide-ranging corpora and annotation work carried out by Global South users. In doing so, the paper argues that generative AI is reigniting long-standing debates in World Englishes about standardization, legitimacy, and the ownership of English, now playing out in algorithmic systems, model training, evaluation practices, and public discourse, where non-dominant Englishes are increasingly conflated with AI-generated speech. Discussing AI systems as a site where language ideologies are (re)produced, the paper argues for more inclusive design approaches that recognize the plurality of Englishes in order to address the real-world negative consequences of treating some as more legitimate than others.
2607.28528.paper_summary_zh: 大型語言模型（LLMs）迅速增長，重新引發了社會語言學和世界英語中的古老問題，例如誰決定什麼算是合法的英語，誰的英語是可疑的等等。這篇論文檢視了AI系統及其使用和相關話語如何反映、強化，並偶爾挑戰（標準）語言意識形態，這些意識形態優先考慮內圈的規範並邊緣化非主流的英語。根據實證研究、媒體評論、社交媒體辯論和AI輸出的例子，這篇論文顯示AI技術在不同層面上再生產主導語言意識形態：訓練數據、設計協議、評估基準、用戶反饋和公共評論。分析利用了圍繞AI語言的公共爭議，特別是對單詞“delve”的執著，來說明來自全球北方的英語使用者如何監控全球南方英語使用者的英語語言規範。這篇論文還指出了Christian Mair所稱的“標準化悖論”：AI可能通過優先考慮標準形式來使英語同質化，同時通過接觸廣泛的語料庫和全球南方用戶進行的標註工作來使英語多元化。在這樣做的過程中，論文主張生成式AI正在重新點燃世界英語中關於標準化、合法性和英語所有權的長期辯論，這些辯論現在在算法系統、模型訓練、評估實踐和公共話語中展開，其中非主流英語越來越與AI生成的語音混淆。討論AI系統作為語言意識形態（再）生產的場所，這篇論文主張採用更具包容性的設計方法，以認識到英語的多樣性，以應對將某些英語視為比其他英語更合法的現實世界負面後果。
2607.28528.author: Kingsley Ugwuanyi et.al.
